Which Kentucky rentals does the statewide act cover?

Not all of them. The uniform act in KRS 383.505 to 383.715 applies only inside cities, counties and urban-county governments that voted to adopt it. KRS 383.500 requires an adopter to use the text word for word, and those governments cannot pass a separate ordinance on the same subjects.

KRS 383.198, added in 2024, also bars any local landlord or tenant ordinance that conflicts with state law. Where the act is not in force, older rules fill the gap. One example is KRS 383.195: a landlord can end a tenancy at will or by sufferance with one month's written notice to leave.

Before you count any notice days below, call city hall or the county clerk and ask whether your community adopted the act. The answer changes which rules govern your tenant.

Security deposits

Under KRS 383.580, a deposit has to be kept apart from the landlord's own money. It goes in an account used only for deposits, at a bank or lending institution regulated by Kentucky or the federal government, and a prospective tenant is told where the account is and its number.

  • Before any deposit changes hands, the landlord gives the tenant a thorough list of existing damage with estimated repair costs, and both sign it.
  • At move-out the landlord inspects again and prepares a final list backing every deduction. The tenant may inspect it, sign it or contest it in writing.
  • If the separate account or either list is missing, the landlord keeps nothing from the deposit.
  • A tenant who disagrees with the final list sues in District Court, limited to the items named in the written dissent.
  • When no rent is owed and a refund is due, the landlord mails notice of the amount. If the tenant stays silent for 60 days, the landlord may keep it.

A tenant who leaves without paying the last month and without asking for the deposit lets the landlord apply it to that debt once 30 days pass. If you are selling, find the account and both damage lists early, because a buyer will ask where the deposit is.

Notice periods for ending a lease or tenancy

The clock depends on the kind of tenancy and the reason it is ending. These are the figures from Chapter 383.

Notice and cure periods in Kentucky landlord and tenant law
SituationRequired period
Week-to-week tenancy (KRS 383.695)Written notice, 7 days before the end date
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice, 30 days ahead of the periodic rental date
Tenancy that began when a written lease endedWritten notice, 10 days before the end date
Rent unpaid (KRS 383.660)Tenant has 7 days after written notice
Material lease breach by tenantTermination at least 14 days after receipt, with a cure window of 15 days
Material breach by landlord (KRS 383.625)Termination at 30 days unless fixed within 14
Landlord visit (KRS 383.615)2 days notice, at reasonable hours

If a tenancy began when a written lease ended and the rent goes unpaid for 10 days past its due date, the landlord may end it with no notice at all. A repeat of substantially the same breach within six months allows termination on 14 days of written notice.

Showing a rented house to buyers

You can, within limits set by KRS 383.615. A tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry that lets the landlord show the unit to prospective or actual purchasers, mortgage lenders, workers or contractors. The landlord gives at least two days' notice and comes at reasonable hours. Emergencies, and cases where notice cannot practicably be given, are exceptions. Using entry to harass the tenant is prohibited.

Outside those situations, entry needs a court order, falls under the abandonment provisions of KRS 383.665 and 383.670, or follows the tenant's surrender of the premises.

If you are preparing to sell a tenant-occupied house, schedule each showing in writing and keep a copy of every notice. A simple log of dates and times protects you if the tenant later complains.

Is a lockout or utility shutoff ever lawful?

KRS 383.690 bars a landlord from retaking the dwelling by action or otherwise, and that includes interrupting heat, electricity, running water, hot water, gas or any other essential service. The narrow exceptions are abandonment, surrender and the remedies the act itself allows.

Possession comes through a forcible detainer case in the District Court for the county where the property sits. A warrant goes to the sheriff or a constable, and a judge hears the case unless one side demands a jury. After a finding for the landlord, the tenant has until the seventh day to file an appeal. If none is filed, the court issues a warrant of restitution directing the sheriff to put the owner back in possession. A forcible detainer inquest cannot be taken more than two years after the act complained of.

Repairs, retaliation and overstays

When a landlord materially breaks the lease or the maintenance duties in KRS 383.595, the tenant may send written notice that the agreement ends in no fewer than 30 days if the problem is still there after 14. A timely fix saves the lease. The tenant can also seek damages and an injunction, and prepaid rent must come back if the agreement ends.

KRS 383.705 shuts down retaliation. After a tenant complains to a housing code agency, complains to the landlord about a violation or joins a tenants' group, the landlord may not raise rent, cut services or file or threaten a possession suit. A complaint made within the prior year creates a presumption that a later move was retaliatory. The landlord can still proceed when the tenant is behind on rent, when the tenant's own carelessness caused the code violation, or when compliance would require work that takes the unit out of use.

A tenant who stays after the lease ends can be sued for possession. If the stay is willful and in bad faith, the landlord may recover the greater of three months' rent or three times actual damages, plus reasonable attorney fees.

How a sale affects the tenant

Chapter 383 has no single rule that a sale ends a lease, so the lease and the sale contract control. A buyer who needs the house empty should plan around the notice that fits the tenancy.

  • Month-to-month: 30 days of written notice before the rental date.
  • Week-to-week: 7 days of written notice.
  • Tenancy running after a written lease expired: 10 days of written notice.

The act excludes occupancy under a contract to buy the unit, so a buyer who moves in before closing is not a tenant under it. Condominium owners living in their own units are excluded too.

Louisville Metro has one more constraint. In a county with a consolidated local government, KRS 383.199 applies to new leases begun after June 27, 2025 on lots in a traditional single-family zone. The owner may not lease the home, a multifamily unit or an accessory dwelling unit unless the owner primarily lives on the lot. A lot with a single home and no accessory unit is outside the rule.

Steps before listing a tenant-occupied house

A short checklist saves weeks later. Pull the lease and any written changes, and find out which notice period fits the tenancy. Confirm where the deposit is held and gather both damage lists. Send showing notices in writing, at least two days ahead.

If you want the tenant gone before closing, count the notice days first and set the closing date after them, not before. If the tenant is staying, tell the buyer up front and let the sale contract say who takes over the lease and the deposit. A cash sale as-is can close around a tenancy, but the buyer will still want the lease and the deposit account shown to them.

Frequently asked questions

How much notice does a monthly rental need before it can end?

Thirty days in writing, counted back from the rental date the notice names. Landlord and tenant use the same period.

What grace does a tenant get after a pay-or-leave notice?

Seven days after the landlord gives written notice of the missed rent and of the intent to terminate. After that the landlord may end the tenancy.

Can a landlord keep a deposit without a move-out damage list?

No. KRS 383.580 bars keeping any of it when the money was not held in a separate account or the starting and ending damage lists were not delivered.

How much warning does a landlord owe before coming in?

At least two days, with entry at reasonable times. Emergencies, and cases where notice is impracticable, are the exceptions.

May a landlord change the locks to force a tenant out?

No. KRS 383.690 prohibits self-help possession, including cutting essential services. The landlord must win a forcible detainer case in District Court.

Notice rules depend on the city or county

Kentucky has no single statewide notice code for residential rentals. KRS 383.500 lets cities, counties and urban-county governments adopt the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, KRS 383.505 to 383.715, but only as a whole and without amendment. The act's notice periods bind only the places that did so.

A number of places have adopted it, including 33 cities counted in a 2017 fiscal note. Louisville, Lexington, Covington, Newport and Florence are among them, as are Oldham County and Pulaski County. Plenty of other towns have not. Phone the clerk for the town or county that holds the house before you pick a notice form.

Notice periods by situation

The table lines up each situation with its period and its statute. Where a row says URLTA, the period applies only in a place that adopted the act.

Notice periods Kentucky landlords look up most often
SituationNotice periodStatute
Rent unpaid (URLTA)Seven days after a notice of nonpayment and intent to terminateKRS 383.660(2)
Other material breach (URLTA)End date no sooner than 14 days after receipt; cure window of 15 daysKRS 383.660(1)
Week-to-week tenancy (URLTA)Seven days before the end dateKRS 383.695(1)
Month-to-month tenancy (URLTA)30 days before the date rent is next dueKRS 383.695(2)
Tenancy after a written lease ends (URLTA)10 days; none if rent is 10 days lateKRS 383.695(3)
Tenancy at will or by sufferance, no URLTAOne monthKRS 383.195
Transfer of a short tenancy without written consent10 days to quitKRS 383.180(2)

Overdue rent in a URLTA place

The tenant gets a week, counted from the landlord's written notice. The notice must say that rent is late and that the landlord intends to end the tenancy if the money does not arrive. A tenant who pays inside that week removes the ground to terminate.

Taking money can undo the notice. Under KRS 383.675, accepting rent with knowledge of the default, or accepting performance that varies from the agreement, waives the right to end the tenancy for that breach unless the parties later agree otherwise. An owner lining up a sale should decide early whether part-payments will be taken.

When the problem is a lease violation, not money

In a URLTA place, the landlord serves a notice that names the acts or omissions and picks an end date at least 14 days after the tenant receives it. If the breach is still open on day 15, the agreement ends as the notice says.

  • A repairable breach is cured if the tenant repairs it or pays for it before the stated end date, and then the agreement continues.
  • The same conduct returning within six months lets the landlord end the agreement on a new 14-day notice with no chance to cure.
  • A tenant who stays on in bad faith after termination risks a judgment for the larger of three months' periodic rent or triple the actual damages, with reasonable lawyer fees added.

Arrangements outside the act

KRS 383.535 lists arrangements the act does not govern, and notices for these follow other rules. Check the list before using a notice form meant for an ordinary apartment lease.

  • Residence at a care, detention or counseling institution when incidental to that service.
  • Occupancy by a buyer under a contract of sale, or by a person who takes over that buyer's interest.
  • Members living in a fraternal or social organization's quarters.
  • Transient stays in a hotel or motel.
  • An employee whose right to live there depends on the job.
  • Condominium owners and cooperative proprietary lease holders.
  • A dwelling on land used for livestock, poultry or crops, including tobacco and timber.

Older rules where the act has not been adopted

Chapter 383's older sections take over. A tenancy at will or by sufferance ends on one month's written notice to remove, and a fixed term simply expires on its date.

A tenant who stays after the term gains no right to remain for 90 days when the term was a year or longer, and for 30 days when it was shorter, and the landlord can start the court case inside those periods without demand or notice. Wait past them and no case can start until a full year (or 60 days, for a shorter term) goes by after the term ends. A city or county cannot pass an ordinance on the subjects the act covers, though ordinances on other housing matters can exist.

How to deliver a Kentucky eviction notice

A tenant receives notice when it is handed over or sent by registered or certified letter to the address the tenant gave for communications, or to the last known home if none was given. A landlord receives notice by a written delivery to the business address used for the rental, or by certified letter there.

Keep a copy, the mailing slip and a dated note of who delivered what. Receipt starts the 14-day count, so mail should leave early enough that the end date still works.

Notice from the tenant

In a URLTA place, KRS 383.695 gives the tenant the same periods the landlord has: seven days for week-to-week, 30 days before the rental date for month-to-month, and 10 days for a tenancy that began when a written lease ended.

A tenant's own notice can empty a house before listing with no court case at all. File it with its date and confirm the move-out date in writing.

What a landlord may not do while a notice runs

A landlord may not take possession by self-help. KRS 383.690 bars regaining the unit by action or otherwise, including shutting off heat, electric power, running water, hot water, gas or another essential service, except for abandonment, surrender or as the act allows.

Retaliation is barred too. After a tenant complains to a code agency, complains to the landlord about a covered violation or joins a tenant group, KRS 383.705 forbids rent hikes, service cuts and threatened possession suits. A complaint made in the prior year creates a presumption of retaliation, yet the landlord may still sue when the tenant is behind on rent.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a notice interacts with selling the rented house

Closing on the house does not by itself end the tenancy. Under KRS 383.600, a seller who conveys in a good faith sale to a bona fide purchaser is freed from liability under the rental agreement for events that follow the tenant's written notice of the conveyance, absent a contrary agreement.

Showings need lead time. KRS 383.615 calls for two days' notice before the landlord enters to display the unit to prospective buyers, at reasonable hours, with emergencies excepted, and a tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry.

  • Decide whether to list with the tenant living there or finish the notice first.
  • Send the tenant written word of the sale once a contract is signed.
  • Ask the closing attorney who will hold the security deposit. KRS 383.580 requires deposits to sit in a separate account and requires damage listings at move-in and move-out.

If the buyer wants the house empty, work backward from the closing date. A 30-day month-to-month notice has to be delivered a full 30 days before the next rent date, and a notice for a lease violation needs at least 14 days after receipt. Build in the days it takes to mail and receive the paper.

Frequently asked questions

What notice must a landlord give for unpaid rent in Kentucky?

Seven days where the URLTA is in force. The landlord gives written word that rent is overdue and that the tenancy will end, and the tenant has a week to pay.

How does a month-to-month tenancy end in Kentucky?

Written notice delivered 30 days before the date rent is next due, from either side, under KRS 383.695(2). Outside URLTA places, one month's written notice ends a tenancy at will.

Can a Kentucky landlord evict with no notice at all?

Only in a narrow case. When a tenancy continues after a written lease and the rent is 10 days late, KRS 383.695(3) lets the landlord end it without notice. Otherwise a written notice comes first.

Can an owner shut off utilities or change locks to push a tenant out?

No. KRS 383.690 forbids recovering possession by interrupting heat, power, water, gas or another essential service. Possession comes through a court order.

Does a sale of the house cancel the lease?

Not by itself. KRS 383.600 only relieves the seller of liability for later events once the tenant has written notice of the conveyance. Read the lease and the sale contract for the rest.
